title: RAYE Announces One-Night Orchestral Show at Royal Albert Hall
excerpt: RAYE will perform her second album, *THIS MUSIC MAY CONTAIN HOPE.*, in full at London's Royal Albert Hall on October 23.
body:
RAYE will perform her second album, *THIS MUSIC MAY CONTAIN HOPE.*, in full at London's Royal Albert Hall on October 23. The one-night show is titled *THIS SYMPHONY MAY CONTAIN HOPE.* and will feature the Heritage Orchestra, Flames Collective choir and her band, with new orchestral arrangements of the songs. It brings her back to the venue where she first presented her music with an orchestra in 2023. This time, however, the album was written with several of those musical elements already in place.

Released in March, *THIS MUSIC MAY CONTAIN HOPE.* unfolds across four seasons, with its music moving from darkness toward hope. Its arrangements draw on jazz, soul, big-band music and orchestral writing. Hans Zimmer worked with RAYE on "Click Clack Symphony." The London Symphony Orchestra and Flames Collective contributed elsewhere. RAYE's first album showed how her older songs could work with an orchestra. The new album comes to the Hall with that approach already embedded in its recordings, although the arrangements for this particular concert will be different.

Her first concert with an orchestra on this scale came in 2023, when she performed music from *My 21st Century Blues* with a 50-piece ensemble and choir at the same venue. The concert was filmed, and the resulting release later received a Grammy nomination for Best Music Film. She returned to the format for a sold-out O2 performance the following year, again working with the same orchestra and choir. The October show will revisit that collaboration, this time with songs from her second album.

RAYE has already shared an example of the new material in an orchestral setting. Released alongside the concert announcement, "I Will Overcome. (Live at Abbey Road Studios)" was recorded with the London Symphony Orchestra. It is a studio performance, not footage from the upcoming concert, and the players are not the same ensemble booked for the Hall. The song comes immediately after the album's brief introduction, and its words are about getting through a painful period. The new version puts that personal song into an arrangement for a full orchestra.

[youtube:Iy2FoVeIUXs]

The second album became RAYE's first UK No. 1 in April, and its hit "WHERE IS MY HUSBAND!" has now crossed one billion Spotify streams. The single occupies the thirteenth spot on a seventeen-song record, leaving a substantial stretch of music after it. Her sisters, Amma and Absolutely, join her on a later song, "Joy." Those family voices sit near the end of a record that opens with RAYE singing about surviving difficult days. A run of quieter songs follows the hit before the album's farewell.

One of the album's distinctive moments comes at the end. "Fin." lasts six minutes and 27 seconds and begins with RAYE speaking directly to the person who has listened all the way through. That address is written into the recording, not improvised for the new concert. She has announced that the performance will include the entire album in order, so the farewell will have the songs leading into it. After the brass, the choir and the changing arrangements, the closing song is addressed to one listener.
